measurements.construction_read: Two 45-degree strokes, each 3 px wide measured horizontally, meeting at a vertex whose lowest pixel is (6,12). Right (ascending) arm runs from tip (12,4) to the junction; left (descending) arm runs from tip (4,8) to the junction. Every stroke end tapers to a single pixel (diamond cap). Arm extents: right arm occupies rows 4-9 above the junction row (6 rows), left arm rows 8-9 (2 rows) plus the shared junction rows 10-12; the long arm is roughly twice the short arm.
measurements.contrast_note: WCAG relative-luminance formula on sRGB values; recorded as a measurement only. The silhouette-readability method states no contrast ratio proves aesthetic quality.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Render a flat mask, inspect proportions/negative space/landmarks at native scale, compare on representative backgrounds; named landmarks must stay visible; a contrast ratio or component count does not prove aesthetic quality.
methods_consulted.applied: Landmarks for a check mark: a short descending arm, a longer ascending arm, a single vertex, and an open acute angle between the arms. All four are visible at 1x on #172336 (views/0001.png) and at 3x (views/0002.png). The mask IS the asset (one flat colour), so the mask test and the colour test coincide. Only the dark panel background is representative here (consumer descriptor); light/busy backgrounds are not a delivery condition.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Trace boundary runs; flag sudden run-length changes; regularise only contours meant to read smooth; preserve intentional corners.
methods_consulted.applied: Both arms are pure 45-degree staircases with a constant one-pixel run; there are no accidental detours. The three one-pixel tips are intentional corners (tapered caps), not jaggies, and must not be 'cleaned'. Edge rhythm is uniform, which suits a UI glyph at 3x nearest where every step becomes a visible 3x3 block.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Extract same-colour components under a declared neighbour rule; intentional details may be legal singletons; component counts are measurements, not verdicts.
methods_consulted.applied: One 4-connected component of 29 pixels; no singletons or stray pixels. The tip pixels belong to the component. This supports the sample-pixel-craft criterion's 'no noisy stray pixels' clause mechanically, while the aesthetic judgement remains visual.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Render at the logical grid, scale by a declared integer with nearest sampling, inspect device pixels; each logical pixel must become a uniform block and no new colours may appear.
methods_consulted.applied: Consumer descriptor declares scale 3 and filter nearest. The retained 48x48 view is byte-identical to a NEAREST 3x enlargement of the #172336 composite and contains exactly two colours, so the retained inspection view satisfies the method's fixture check. The live renderer's behaviour (DPR, CSS zoom, non-integer scaling) remains unverified because none is supplied.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Declare alpha policy separately from palette; composite consistently through export/import/display; binary-alpha assets contain only 0 and 255 unless an exception is declared.
methods_consulted.applied: The contract declares alpha 'full' (partial alpha permitted) because BRIEF.md requires transparency but does not restrict alpha levels. The delivered fixture is binary (0/255), so straight vs. premultiplied compositing cannot produce fringe differences on this sample. That is an observed property of the sample, not a tightening of the contract.

methods_consulted.what_it_says: Map states to explicit visuals; use timing only for events that occurred; retain static recognisability; no decorative timer may report progress that has not happened.
methods_consulted.applied: Ready is the visual for succeeded, reached via stateAfter('ok'); it is static (frames 1) and carries no motion, so it cannot falsely report activity. verify-integration.mjs exercised exactly this mapping through both consumers. The method's pitfall about imported project palettes applies: #70b9ed is this project's observed accent, not a universal rule.

pixel_art_assessment.readability_1x_3x_verdict_specialist: Reads as a check mark with clearly unequal arms at both scales on the actual panel colour; no essential detail merges into the panel. This agrees with the retained verdicts; it is a fresh specialist reading and does not alter the retained verdict records.
pixel_art_assessment.composition_observation: The glyph's bounding box is one pixel right of and one pixel below the geometric cell centre (margins L3/R2/T4/B3). For a check mark whose visual mass sits in the long right arm this slight right/down bias is a common optical-centering outcome and is not a defect under any owner criterion. For comparison the Start triangle spans x 4-14, y 2-14 in SVG units (bbox centre (9,8)); Ready's bbox centre is (8.5,8.5). Family alignment is a later-stage check.
pixel_art_assessment.family_extensibility_opinion_proposal: The treatment is a minimal vocabulary: one flat cool-blue tone, 3-px-wide 45-degree strokes, one-pixel tapered caps, no plate or outline. It extends plausibly: Working as four phases of a 3-px arc/segment rotating in the same cell; Retry as a circular arrow in the same stroke; Paused as two 3-px vertical bars. Because the tone is flat, every family distinction must come from shape, which is exactly what BRIEF.md lines 3 and 7 require (non-colour distinguishability). This is an expert proposal for the style decision, not a requirement and not an approval.
risks_noted: A single flat tone leaves no internal contrast hierarchy; if the owner later wants a highlight or shade (as the FIRST request described), that is a style decision to make before family production, not a retrofit.
At 1x on a dark panel, the 1-px tips are the first detail to disappear on low-quality displays; they survive at 3x. Acceptable for a status glyph; note for Retry/Paused design.
Fixture provenance: none of these craft properties can be assumed for live PixelLab output; a live sample would need the same inspection.
